title: Rep. David Valadao highlights school program visit and new veteran care legislation - Kern County Times
text:
Rep. David Valadao, U.S. Congressman representing California’s 22nd district since 2021, recently highlighted his involvement in local education and veteran support initiatives through a series of posts on social media.
On January 13, Valadao shared that his team attended a school event in Shafter: “Today, Team Valadao joined Redwood Elementary for the groundbreaking of their Expanded Opportunities Learning Program in Shafter. This program offers students an opportunity to build friendships and gain life skills outside the classroom, and my staff was honored to attend.”
The following day, he posted about legislative efforts aimed at assisting veterans. In one post dated January 14, Valadao stated: “This bill helps ensure vulnerable veterans don’t slip through the cracks by strengthening VA coordination and accountability and helping connect them with the benefits they’ve earned.” On the same day, he also announced the reintroduction of legislation focused on homeless veterans: “After serving our nation, veterans deserve timely access to quality care, including stable housing and mental health support when needed. That’s why I’m proud to reintroduce the Improving Mental Health Care and Coordination for Homeless Veterans Act.”
Valadao has represented California’s 22nd District since defeating former Congressman TJ Cox in 2021. He previously served in the California State Assembly from 2010 to 2012. Born in Hanford, California in 1977, Valadao continues to reside there while serving his congressional district.
